{"parentUuid":"923717e0-f506-4482-91fc-ee25174af891","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b4782d42-f54b-404f-bbf6-049a33d49a2c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01H8o54mtArA7Xwnn4dfnjRD","type":"tool_result","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nASA, the African Student Association at Kenyon, is described in the client brief as a student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. Students need an easy way to find event announcements (including an Afrobeat event), learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Its leaders need event announcements to be quick to publish, information about ASA to stay easy to find in the navigation, and a way to share photos only when ASA has permission to use them. One ASA leader should manage accounts and permanent pages; another member should be able to write and update event posts without a complicated form.\n\nThis is a class project (IPHS 400, Mini-Project #2). No claim is made about any real ASA process, officers, schedule or history. Terms below are defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS. A local admin console lets an Admin and Editors write **Posts** and **Pages**, manage accounts, and preview content. A `cms publish` step renders only **Published** content into a static public site, and `cms deploy` sends it to GitHub Pages, at which point the content is **Live**. The admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001).\n\nThe public site has a **Home page** (a short **Welcome text** taken from the client brief plus the five latest **Announcements**), an **Announcements** list, and **Navigation** built from published Pages (starter Pages for the demo: About ASA, Resources, Photos). Event announcements are ordinary Posts with the event's date, time, location and who can attend written in the **Body**. Photos are images inside Posts or Pages; there is no upload form.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Signing in\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with a username and password, so that only authorised people can change the site.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in and out, so that my session ends when I leave a shared computer.\n3. As an account owner, I want my password stored hashed, so that nobody, including the Admin, can read it.\n4. As an Admin, I want a wrong password to be rejected with a clear message that does not reveal whether the username exists, so that accounts cannot be guessed.\n5. As someone with a Deactivated account, I want sign-in to be refused, so that a former member can no longer change the site.\n6. As a signed-in user, I want every form I submit to be protected against forged requests, so that another website cannot act as me.\n7. As a visitor who is not signed in, I want any admin address to send me to sign-in, so that I never see admin content.\n\n### First Admin and setup\n8. As the project owner, I want the first Admin account created from the command line with a password taken from the environment, so that no password is committed to Git.\n9. As the project owner, I want a clean clone to run from `.env.example` plus a few documented steps, so that a grader can reproduce the demo.\n10. As the project owner, I want the database and `.env` kept out of Git, so that private data is never published.\n11. As the project owner, I want demo data that can be rebuilt on demand, so that screenshots and tests are repeatable.\n\n### Roles and permission refusal\n12. As an Admin, I want to manage accounts and permanent Pages, so that I control who can change the site and what the Navigation contains.\n13. As an Editor, I want to create and publish Posts directly, so that an announcement can go out quickly.\n14. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including another Editor's, so that event details can be corrected close to the event if the writer is unavailable.\n15. As an Editor, I want to update the Body of an existing Page, so that the Photos page can stay current.\n16. As an Admin, I want only Admins to delete Posts, so that a mistaken deletion is unlikely.\n17. As an Admin, I want only Admins to create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page, so that Navigation and links stay stable.\n18. As an Admin, I want only Admins to change a slug, and to be warned that doing so can break an old link, so that shared links keep working.\n19. As an Editor, I want admin-only controls hidden from my screens, so that my screens stay simple.\n20. As an Editor who reaches an Admin-only address or submits a forbidden action directly, I want a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard, so that I understand what happened.\n21. As an Admin, I want every permission enforced by the server, not by hidden buttons, so that access control is real.\n\n### Posts\n22. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Body and save it as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it is ready for the public site.\n24. As an Editor, I want to unpublish a Post, so that a wrong announcement stops going out.\n25. As an Editor, I want the slug generated from my title on first save, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n26. As an Editor, I want a number added automatically when a slug already exists, so that two Posts never collide.\n27. As an Editor, I want the slug to stay unchanged when I correct the title or event details, so that shared links keep working.\n28. As an Editor, I want a short hint reminding me to include What, When, Where and Who can attend, so that announcements are complete.\n29. As an Editor, I want the hint not pre-filled into the Body and hideable without losing content, so that I can write naturally.\n30. As an Editor, I want the Post to record me as its Author automatically, so that I do not fill in extra fields.\n31. As an Editor, I want the Post's created, updated and first-published times recorded automatically, so that dates are trustworthy.\n\n### Pages\n32. As an Admin, I want to create a Page with a title, slug and Body, so that permanent information has a home.\n33. As an Admin, I want a published Page to appear in the public Navigation automatically, so that visitors can find it.\n34. As an Admin, I want an unpublished Page to disappear from the Navigation, so that unfinished pages are not linked.\n35. As an Admin, I want to delete a Page, so that obsolete pages can be removed.\n36. As an Editor, I want to edit the Body of a Page but see title, slug, status and delete controls as unavailable, so that I cannot break the Navigation.\n\n### Writing, preview and images\n37. As an Editor, I want to use headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text, so that announcements read well without learning HTML.\n38. As an Editor, I want raw HTML, scripts, frames and forms in my text stripped, so that the site is safe.\n39. As an Editor, I want a preview that shows exactly what the public page will render, so that there are no surprises after publishing.\n40. As an Editor, I want to write a caption, alt text and Markdown reference for an image, so that photos are accessible.\n41. As an Editor, I understand I cannot add a new image file myself, so that the release-holder can confirm Photo permission first.\n42. As the release-holder, I want approved image files copied into the public site with relative paths, so that photos show up after deployment.\n43. As the release-holder, I want demo illustrations labelled as illustrative and never presented as photos of real ASA events, so that visitors are not misled.\n\n### Admin console\n44. As an Admin, I want a dashboard with the counts of Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As an Admin, I want the dashboard to also show the number of active and Deactivated accounts, so that I can keep track of who has access.\n46. As an Editor, I want the dashboard to show the four content counts but no account counts, so that I only see what I need.\n47. As any signed-in user, I want a reminder on the dashboard that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run, so that I do not expect instant changes.\n48. As any signed-in user, I want one Content list I can filter by Post or Page and by Draft or Published, so that I can find content without opening each item.\n49. As any signed-in user, I want each row to show title, status, Display name and last-updated time, so that I can tell items apart.\n50. As a phone user, I want the admin console usable at phone width, so that I can post from anywhere.\n\n### User management\n51. As an Admin, I want to create an account with a username, a private password, a role and a public Display name, so that a new member can start writing.\n52. As an Admin, I want to change an account's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n53. As an Admin, I want to deactivate an account, so that a former member can no longer sign in while their published Posts stay.\n54. As an Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated account, so that a mistake is recoverable.\n55. As an Admin, I want to set a new password for an existing account without seeing the old one, so that a lost password can be recovered.\n56. As an Admin, I want a reset password never printed or logged, so that it cannot leak.\n57. As an Admin, I want to change an account's Display name, so that a former member can ask for their name to be replaced with \"ASA Events Team\".\n58. As an Admin, I want the original Author link of every Post kept, even after a Display name change or deactivation, so that the record stays accurate.\n59. As an Admin, I want the private username never used as a byline by default, so that private account names do not appear publicly.\n60. As an Admin, I want accounts deactivated rather than deleted, so that history is preserved.\n\n### Public site\n61. As a first-time visitor, I want a short welcome on the Home page, so that I know what ASA is and that I am welcome.\n62. As a visitor, I want the five latest Announcements on the Home page with a link to all of them, so that I can see what is new.\n63. As a visitor, I want an Announcements page listing all Published Posts, newest first by first-published date, so that I can browse.\n64. As a visitor, I want each Announcement as a clear Event card showing its title, first-published date and byline, so that I can scan quickly on a phone.\n65. As a visitor, I want an \"Updated\" date on a card when the content changed after first publishing, so that I know details were corrected.\n66. As a visitor, I want the event's actual date, time, location and who can attend in the Body, and the publication date never labelled as the event date, so that I am not misled.\n67. As a visitor, I want a Post to keep its original first-published date if it is unpublished and later published again, so that the order is stable.\n68. As a visitor, I want the Navigation to list Announcements and every published Page (About ASA, Resources, Photos for the demo), so that information is easy to find.\n69. As a visitor, I want the Photos page to say that actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them, so that placeholders are not mistaken for real events.\n70. As a visitor, I want the public site to work on a phone with readable text, so that I can use it anywhere.\n71. As a visitor who uses a keyboard or screen reader, I want a sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus, keyboard access to all controls, and alt text on every image, so that the site is accessible.\n72. As a visitor, I want Drafts and unpublished content never to appear anywhere in the public site, so that unfinished work stays private.\n73. As a visitor, I want the site to work from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no link or style is broken.\n\n### Releasing\n74. As the release-holder, I want `cms publish` to write the public site from Published content only, so that Drafts never leave the database.\n75. As the release-holder, I want `cms deploy` to send the result to GitHub Pages, so that content becomes Live.\n76. As the release-holder, I want a short release checklist covering publish, deploy, checking relative paths, adding approved images, and confirming Photo permission, so that the step is quick and repeatable.\n77. As the release-holder, I want the checklist to state that an Editor cannot add an image file alone, so that clients are not surprised.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture is fixed** by ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site) and ADR-002 (FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2, Markdown sanitizer). No new dependencies.\n- **Content model.** Two kinds of content only: Post and Page. No separate Event type and no event-date field. A Post has a title, slug, Markdown Body, status (Draft or Published), Author, and created, updated and first-published times. A Page has the same fields except that the Author is optional for display and a Page does not appear in the Announcements list.\n- **First-published date** is set the first time a Post becomes Published and never cleared, including when the Post is unpublished and republished. The **Updated date** on the public card is shown when the Body or title changes after the first-published date.\n- **Ordering.** Announcements are ordered by first-published date, newest first. Editing does not reorder. The Home page shows the five most recent; the Announcements page shows all Published Posts.\n- **Slugs.** A Post's slug is generated from its title on first save, made unique by adding a number, and never changed automatically. A Page's slug is entered by the Admin. Only the Admin can change any slug, and the form warns that this can break existing links. Slug edits are not shown to Editors.\n- **Accounts.** An account has a private username, a password hash, a role (Admin or Editor), a public Display name, and an active flag. There is no account deletion. Posts keep their Author link permanently. A Post's public byline is the Author's current Display name. The username is never used as a byline.\n- **Authentication.** Session cookie signed by the server. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and are never stored, shown or logged in plain form. Sign-in failures use one generic message. A Deactivated account cannot sign in and any existing session for it stops working.\n- **Authorization.** A single central rule table maps each action to the roles allowed. Every state-changing route checks it on the server. Templates hide controls the current role cannot use, but hiding is never the protection. A refused action shows a \"You don't have permission\" page with a link to the dashboard, and a not-signed-in visitor is sent to sign-in.\n- **Permission matrix.** Admin: everything. Editor: sign in and out; create, edit and publish or unpublish Posts, including other people's; edit the Body of an existing Page; view dashboard counts and the Content list. Editor cannot: delete Posts or Pages; create, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug Pages; change any slug; open user management or change any account, role or Display name; reset passwords.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies.\n- **Markdown and sanitizing.** Allowed: headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms are stripped. The same rendering and sanitizing path is used for the admin preview and the public export, so the preview matches the public page.\n- **Images.** No upload feature. Approved image files are added to the project by the release-holder and copied into the public site by `cms publish`. Markdown references use relative paths. Demo illustrations are clearly labelled illustrative.\n- **Admin console screens.** Sign-in, Dashboard, Content list, Post editor with Preview and the Event details hint, Page editor (reduced controls for Editors), User management (Admin only), and the permission-refusal page. Layouts work at phone width.\n- **Dashboard.** Four content counts for everyone; active and deactivated account counts for the Admin only; a reminder that Published is not Live. No \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- **Content list.** One list of Posts and Pages, filterable by type and by status, with title, status, Display name and last-updated time on each row.\n- **Event details hint.** A short, dismissible hint near the Post editor listing What, When, Where and Who can attend. It is never inserted into the Body.\n- **Publishing.** `cms publish` renders Home, Announcements, each Published Post, each Published Page and the Navigation to plain HTML, using only Published content and only relative paths. It copies approved image files. `cms deploy` pushes the result to the `gh-pages` branch. Nothing is Live until both have run.\n- **Public design.** Polished, mobile-first, readable text, clear Event cards, a few appropriately licensed images or decorative graphics that are never presented as real ASA event photos. Accessibility requirements: sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus and full keyboard access, phone-width layout, and alt text on every image.\n- **Content carried from the client brief.** The Welcome text uses only the brief's wording. Starter Pages (About ASA, Resources, Photos) and seed Posts are demo placeholders and contain no claims about ASA's real history, officers, members, schedule or approval process.\n- **First Admin.** Created from the command line at setup, with the password read from the environment. No password, `.env` or database file is committed. A clean clone runs from `.env.example` plus documented steps.\n- **Demo data.** The seed data is rebuilt on demand and includes both roles, published and draft Posts and Pages, and a deactivated account.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a signed-in user sees and can do, and what files the publish step writes. It does not check internal functions, the database layout or template details.\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** Use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. Cover sign-in and sign-out, Deactivated accounts, each row of the permission matrix (both the allowed and the refused case, for every Admin-only action), CSRF rejection, Post and Page create/read/update/delete, slug generation and stability, First-published date rules, Dashboard counts by role, Content list filtering, Preview matching public output, user management and Password reset, and Display name changes.\n- **Seam 2: the published site on disk.** Call the publish step against seeded data into a temporary folder and read the HTML files. Cover: Drafts and unpublished content absent; sanitized Markdown (raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms stripped); Navigation built from published Pages; Announcements ordering and the five-item Home page; byline uses the Display name and never the username; \"Updated\" date shown after later edits; only relative `href` and `src` values; approved image files copied; the Welcome text present.\n- **Seam 3 (small smoke test): the `cms` command.** First-Admin creation from an environment password, and a clean-setup run from `.env.example`. Kept small and separate.\n- **Prior art.** `tests/conftest.py` already provides the app and `client_as` fixtures, and the walking-skeleton test shows the style. Access-control tests should follow the one-line pattern in the `conftest.py` docstring.\n- **Test-first.** Each ticket starts with failing tests. Read the tests before letting them pass, to catch a test written against a misunderstanding.\n- **Security checks.** Drafts never appear in the export, no plain password in any response or log, no root-absolute paths in the export, sanitized output, CSRF on every state-changing form, and server-side enforcement of every Admin-only action.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Release checklist.** Written as part of the project. It covers running publish and deploy, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. For the class demo the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n- **Photo permission** is a working rule for this project, not a known ASA policy.\n- **ADRs.** No new ADR was needed from the grill. Add one later only if a decision is hard to reverse and surprising.\n- **Vocabulary.** Use the terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Post, Announcements, Event announcement, Page, Published, Live, Display name, Username, Deactivated account, Permission refusal, and so on). Do not use \"Upcoming Events\" for the Announcements list.\n\n----\nASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. The website should make it easy for students to find upcoming events, including an Afrobeat event, learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Event announcements should be quick to publish, while information about ASA and its resources should remain easy to find in the navigation. An ASA leader would manage accounts and permanent pages; another member could write and update event posts. The site should feel welcoming to someone discovering ASA for the first time. Photos should only be published when ASA has permission to use Association at Kenyon, is described in the client brief as a student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. Students need an easy way to find event announcements (including an Afrobeat event), learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Its leaders need event announcements to be quick to publish, information about ASA to stay easy to find in the navigation, and a way to share photos only when ASA has permission to use them. One ASA leader should manage accounts and permanent pages; another member should be able to write and update event posts without a complicated form.\n\nThis is a class project (IPHS 400, Mini-Project #2). No claim is made about any real ASA process, officers, schedule or history. Terms below are defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS. A local admin console lets an Admin and Editors write **Posts** and **Pages**, manage accounts, and preview content. A `cms publish` step renders only **Published** content into a static public site, and `cms deploy` sends it to GitHub Pages, at which point the content is **Live**. The admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001).\n\nThe public site has a **Home page** (a short **Welcome text** taken from the client brief plus the five latest **Announcements**), an **Announcements** list, and **Navigation** built from published Pages (starter Pages for the demo: About ASA, Resources, Photos). Event announcements are ordinary Posts with the event's date, time, location and who can attend written in the **Body**. Photos are images inside Posts or Pages; there is no upload form.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Signing in\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with a username and password, so that only authorised people can change the site.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in and out, so that my session ends when I leave a shared computer.\n3. As an account owner, I want my password stored hashed, so that nobody, including the Admin, can read it.\n4. As an Admin, I want a wrong password to be rejected with a clear message that does not reveal whether the username exists, so that accounts cannot be guessed.\n5. As someone with a Deactivated account, I want sign-in to be refused, so that a former member can no longer change the site.\n6. As a signed-in user, I want every form I submit to be protected against forged requests, so that another website cannot act as me.\n7. As a visitor who is not signed in, I want any admin address to send me to sign-in, so that I never see admin content.\n\n### First Admin and setup\n8. As the project owner, I want the first Admin account created from the command line with a password taken from the environment, so that no password is committed to Git.\n9. As the project owner, I want a clean clone to run from `.env.example` plus a few documented steps, so that a grader can reproduce the demo.\n10. As the project owner, I want the database and `.env` kept out of Git, so that private data is never published.\n11. As the project owner, I want demo data that can be rebuilt on demand, so that screenshots and tests are repeatable.\n\n### Roles and permission refusal\n12. As an Admin, I want to manage accounts and permanent Pages, so that I control who can change the site and what the Navigation contains.\n13. As an Editor, I want to create and publish Posts directly, so that an announcement can go out quickly.\n14. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including another Editor's, so that event details can be corrected close to the event if the writer is unavailable.\n15. As an Editor, I want to update the Body of an existing Page, so that the Photos page can stay current.\n16. As an Admin, I want only Admins to delete Posts, so that a mistaken deletion is unlikely.\n17. As an Admin, I want only Admins to create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page, so that Navigation and links stay stable.\n18. As an Admin, I want only Admins to change a slug, and to be warned that doing so can break an old link, so that shared links keep working.\n19. As an Editor, I want admin-only controls hidden from my screens, so that my screens stay simple.\n20. As an Editor who reaches an Admin-only address or submits a forbidden action directly, I want a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard, so that I understand what happened.\n21. As an Admin, I want every permission enforced by the server, not by hidden buttons, so that access control is real.\n\n### Posts\n22. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Body and save it as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it is ready for the public site.\n24. As an Editor, I want to unpublish a Post, so that a wrong announcement stops going out.\n25. As an Editor, I want the slug generated from my title on first save, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n26. As an Editor, I want a number added automatically when a slug already exists, so that two Posts never collide.\n27. As an Editor, I want the slug to stay unchanged when I correct the title or event details, so that shared links keep working.\n28. As an Editor, I want a short hint reminding me to include What, When, Where and Who can attend, so that announcements are complete.\n29. As an Editor, I want the hint not pre-filled into the Body and hideable without losing content, so that I can write naturally.\n30. As an Editor, I want the Post to record me as its Author automatically, so that I do not fill in extra fields.\n31. As an Editor, I want the Post's created, updated and first-published times recorded automatically, so that dates are trustworthy.\n\n### Pages\n32. As an Admin, I want to create a Page with a title, slug and Body, so that permanent information has a home.\n33. As an Admin, I want a published Page to appear in the public Navigation automatically, so that visitors can find it.\n34. As an Admin, I want an unpublished Page to disappear from the Navigation, so that unfinished pages are not linked.\n35. As an Admin, I want to delete a Page, so that obsolete pages can be removed.\n36. As an Editor, I want to edit the Body of a Page but see title, slug, status and delete controls as unavailable, so that I cannot break the Navigation.\n\n### Writing, preview and images\n37. As an Editor, I want to use headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text, so that announcements read well without learning HTML.\n38. As an Editor, I want raw HTML, scripts, frames and forms in my text stripped, so that the site is safe.\n39. As an Editor, I want a preview that shows exactly what the public page will render, so that there are no surprises after publishing.\n40. As an Editor, I want to write a caption, alt text and Markdown reference for an image, so that photos are accessible.\n41. As an Editor, I understand I cannot add a new image file myself, so that the release-holder can confirm Photo permission first.\n42. As the release-holder, I want approved image files copied into the public site with relative paths, so that photos show up after deployment.\n43. As the release-holder, I want demo illustrations labelled as illustrative and never presented as photos of real ASA events, so that visitors are not misled.\n\n### Admin console\n44. As an Admin, I want a dashboard with the counts of Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As an Admin, I want the dashboard to also show the number of active and Deactivated accounts, so that I can keep track of who has access.\n46. As an Editor, I want the dashboard to show the four content counts but no account counts, so that I only see what I need.\n47. As any signed-in user, I want a reminder on the dashboard that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run, so that I do not expect instant changes.\n48. As any signed-in user, I want one Content list I can filter by Post or Page and by Draft or Published, so that I can find content without opening each item.\n49. As any signed-in user, I want each row to show title, status, Display name and last-updated time, so that I can tell items apart.\n50. As a phone user, I want the admin console usable at phone width, so that I can post from anywhere.\n\n### User management\n51. As an Admin, I want to create an account with a username, a private password, a role and a public Display name, so that a new member can start writing.\n52. As an Admin, I want to change an account's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n53. As an Admin, I want to deactivate an account, so that a former member can no longer sign in while their published Posts stay.\n54. As an Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated account, so that a mistake is recoverable.\n55. As an Admin, I want to set a new password for an existing account without seeing the old one, so that a lost password can be recovered.\n56. As an Admin, I want a reset password never printed or logged, so that it cannot leak.\n57. As an Admin, I want to change an account's Display name, so that a former member can ask for their name to be replaced with \"ASA Events Team\".\n58. As an Admin, I want the original Author link of every Post kept, even after a Display name change or deactivation, so that the record stays accurate.\n59. As an Admin, I want the private username never used as a byline by default, so that private account names do not appear publicly.\n60. As an Admin, I want accounts deactivated rather than deleted, so that history is preserved.\n\n### Public site\n61. As a first-time visitor, I want a short welcome on the Home page, so that I know what ASA is and that I am welcome.\n62. As a visitor, I want the five latest Announcements on the Home page with a link to all of them, so that I can see what is new.\n63. As a visitor, I want an Announcements page listing all Published Posts, newest first by first-published date, so that I can browse.\n64. As a visitor, I want each Announcement as a clear Event card showing its title, first-published date and byline, so that I can scan quickly on a phone.\n65. As a visitor, I want an \"Updated\" date on a card when the content changed after first publishing, so that I know details were corrected.\n66. As a visitor, I want the event's actual date, time, location and who can attend in the Body, and the publication date never labelled as the event date, so that I am not misled.\n67. As a visitor, I want a Post to keep its original first-published date if it is unpublished and later published again, so that the order is stable.\n68. As a visitor, I want the Navigation to list Announcements and every published Page (About ASA, Resources, Photos for the demo), so that information is easy to find.\n69. As a visitor, I want the Photos page to say that actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them, so that placeholders are not mistaken for real events.\n70. As a visitor, I want the public site to work on a phone with readable text, so that I can use it anywhere.\n71. As a visitor who uses a keyboard or screen reader, I want a sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus, keyboard access to all controls, and alt text on every image, so that the site is accessible.\n72. As a visitor, I want Drafts and unpublished content never to appear anywhere in the public site, so that unfinished work stays private.\n73. As a visitor, I want the site to work from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no link or style is broken.\n\n### Releasing\n74. As the release-holder, I want `cms publish` to write the public site from Published content only, so that Drafts never leave the database.\n75. As the release-holder, I want `cms deploy` to send the result to GitHub Pages, so that content becomes Live.\n76. As the release-holder, I want a short release checklist covering publish, deploy, checking relative paths, adding approved images, and confirming Photo permission, so that the step is quick and repeatable.\n77. Starter Pages (About ASA, Resources, Photos) and seed Posts are demo placeholders and contain no claims about ASA's real history, officers, members, schedule or approval process.\n- **First Admin.** Created from the command line at setup, with the password read from the environment. No password, `.env` or database file is committed. A clean clone runs from `.env.example` plus documented steps.\n- **Demo data.** The seed data is rebuilt on demand and includes both roles, published and draft Posts and Pages, and a deactivated account.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a signed-in user sees and can do, and what files the publish step writes. It does not check internal functions, the database layout or template details.\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** Use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. Cover sign-in and sign-out, Deactivated accounts, each row of the permission matrix (both the allowed and the refused case, for every Admin-only action), CSRF rejection, Post and Page create/read/update/delete, slug generation and stability, First-published date rules, Dashboard counts by role, Content list filtering, Preview matching public output, user management and Password reset, and Display name changes.\n- **Seam 2: the published site on disk.** Call the publish step against seeded data into a temporary folder and read the HTML files. Cover: Drafts and unpublished content absent; sanitized Markdown (raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms stripped); Navigation built from published Pages; Announcements ordering and the five-item Home page; byline uses the Display name and never the username; \"Updated\" date shown after later edits; only relative `href` and `src` values; approved image files copied; the Welcome text present.\n- **Seam 3 (small smoke test): the `cms` command.** First-Admin creation from an environment password, and a clean-setup run from `.env.example`. Kept small and separate.\n- **Prior art.** `tests/conftest.py` already provides the app and `client_as` fixtures, and the walking-skeleton test shows the style. Access-control tests should follow the one-line pattern in the `conftest.py` docstring.\n- **Test-first.** Each ticket starts with failing tests. Read the tests before letting them pass, to catch a test written against a misunderstanding.\n- **Security checks.** Drafts never appear in the export, no plain password in any response or log, no root-absolute paths in the export, sanitized output, CSRF on every state-changing form, and server-side enforcement of every Admin-only action.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Release checklist.** Written as part of the project. It covers running publish and deploy, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. For the class demo the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n- **Photo permission** is a working rule for this project, not a known ASA policy.\n- **ADRs.** No new ADR was needed from the grill. Add one later only if a decision is hard to reverse and surprising.\n- **Vocabulary.** Use the terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Post, Announcements, Event announcement, Page, Published, Live, Display name, Username, Deactivated account, Permission refusal, and so on). Do not use \"Upcoming Events\" for the Announcements list.\n\n----\nASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. The website should make it easy for students to find upcoming events, including an Afrobeat event, learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Event announcements should be quick to publish, while information about ASA and its resources should remain easy to find in the navigation. An ASA leader would manage accounts and permanent pages; another member could write and update event posts. The site should feel welcoming to someone discovering ASA for the first time. Photos should only be published when ASA has permission to use {"parentUuid":"4f0fb280-7b22-4208-8f41-98e40a2d100f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b4782d42-f54b-404f-bbf6-049a33d49a2c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Rh6YqX9vaF51qJ529ZRBLJ","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nTwo rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     Pages one folder down (posts/) reach the site root with a `root` of \"../\".\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import closing\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import pages, settings\nfrom app.db import connect\nfrom app.rendering import render_body\n\n# The wording comes from notes/client-brief.md. Make no other claim about ASA.\nWELCOME = (\n    \"ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students \"\n    \"with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African \"\n    \"cultures and community.\"\n)\nHOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS = 5\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem 1.5rem; align-items: baseline; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\na:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\nimg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }\n.card { border: 1px solid; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; margin-block: 1rem; }\n.card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.2rem; }\n.meta { margin: 0.25rem 0 0; font-size: 0.9rem; opacity: 0.8; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef _day(timestamp: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"A stored UTC timestamp as (\"2026-09-28\", \"28 September 2026\").\"\"\"\n    moment = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp)\n    return moment.date().isoformat(), f\"{moment.day} {moment:%B %Y}\"\n\n\ndef _published_posts(database: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Published Posts only, newest First-published date first.\n\n    Ordered by First-published date, not by edit time, so a correction never\n    moves a Post. The byline is the Author's Display name; the Username is not\n    even selected.\n    \"\"\"\n    with closing(connect(database)) as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT posts.title, posts.slug, posts.body, posts.updated_at, \"\n            \"posts.first_published_at, users.display_name AS author_name \"\n            \"FROM posts JOIN users ON users.id = posts.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE posts.status = 'published' \"\n            \"ORDER BY posts.first_published_at DESC, posts.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    return [_post_for_template(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef _post_for_template(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:\n    posted_iso, posted_label = _day(row[\"first_published_at\"])\n    post = {\n        \"title\": row[\"title\"], \"slug\": row[\"slug\"], \"author_name\": row[\"author_name\"],\n        \"body_html\": render_body(row[\"body\"]),\n        \"posted_iso\": posted_iso, \"posted_label\": posted_label,\n        \"updated_iso\": None, \"updated_label\": None,\n    }\n    if row[\"updated_at\"] > row[\"first_published_at\"]:\n        post[\"updated_iso\"], post[\"updated_label\"] = _day(row[\"updated_at\"])\n    return post\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None, database: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    database = database or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    (out / \"posts\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    published = _published_posts(database)\n    published_pages = pages.list_published(database)\n    # Every page of the site shows the same Navigation; the template prefixes `root`.\n    nav_pages = [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"slug\": page[\"slug\"]} for page in published_pages]\n    common = {\"site_title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"nav_pages\": nav_pages}\n\n    def write(name: str, template: str, **context) -> None:\n        (out / name).write_text(env.get_template(template).render(\n            **common, **context))\n\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    write(\"index.html\", \"public/home.html\", title=settings.SITE_TITLE, root=\"\",\n          welcome=WELCOME, posts=published[:HOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS])\n    write(\"announcements.html\", \"public/announcements.html\",\n          title=f\"Announcements · {settings.SITE_TITLE}\", root=\"\", posts=published)\n    for post in published:\n        write(f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\", \"public/post.html\", root=\"../\", post=post,\n              title=post[\"title\"])\n    for page in published_pages:\n        write(f\"{page['slug']}.html\", \"public/page.html\", root=\"\", title=page[\"title\"],\n              page={\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"body_html\": render_body(page[\"body\"])})\n    return out\n\"\"\"Markdown Body -> safe HTML. The one path for the public export and, later, Preview.\n\nRaw HTML is let through the Markdown parser and then removed by the sanitizer,\nso `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<form>` and event handlers never survive. students and students with African backgrounds\"\n\n\ndef author_id(db_path, username=\"editor\"):\n    with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT id FROM users WHERE title=title, body=body,\n                           author_id=author_id(db_path, by))\n    if published:\n        posts.publish(db_path, post_id)\n    return post_id\n\n\ndef site_files(out):\n    return sorted(p for p in out.rglob(\"*\") if p.is_file())\n\n\ndef all_text(out):\n    return \"\\n\".join(p.read_text() for p in site_files(out)\n                     if p.suffix in (\".html\", \".css\"))\n\n\ndef html_files(out):\n    return [p for p in site_files(out) if p.suffix == \".html\"]\n\n\ndef read(out, name):\n    return (out / name).read_text()\n\n\ndef titles_in_order(html):\n    \"\"\"The Event card titles in the order they appear on the page.\"\"\"\n    return re.findall(r'<h2 class=\"card-title\"><a [^>]*>([^<]+)</a>', html)\n\n\ndef publish(db_path, tmp_path):\n    return render_site(tmp_path / \"site\", database=db_path)\n\n\n# -- what is written ---------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_publish_writes_home_announcements_and_one_page_per_post(db_path, tmp_path):\n    add_post(db_path, \"Afrobeat Night\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Movie Evening\")\n    out = publish(db_path, tmp_path)\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists()\n    assert (out / \"announcements.html\").exists()\n    assert (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n    assert \"Afrobeat Night\" in read(out, \"posts/afrobeat-night.html\")\n    assert \"Movie Evening\" in read(out, \"posts/movie-evening.html\")\n\n\ndef test_home_page_has_the_welcome_text(db_path, tmp_path):\n    out = publish(db_path, tmp_path)\n    assert WELCOME in read(out, \"index.html\")\n\n\ndef test_home_shows_the_five_latest_and_links_to_all_announcements(db_path, tmp_path):\n    for n in range(1, 8):\n        add_post(db_path, f\"Post number {n}\")\n    out = publish(db_path, tmp_path)\n    home = read(out, \"index.html\")\n    assert titles_in_order(home) == [f\"Post number {n}\" for n in (7, 6, 5, 4,  \"[//host](//evil.example/x) [web](https://example.org)\"\n    add_post(db_path, \"Links Post\", body)\n    add_post(db_path, \"Another\")\n    out = publish(db_path, tmp_path)\n    found = 0\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        for value in re.findall(r'(?:href|src)=\"([^\"]*)\"', path.read_text()):\n            found += 1\n            assert not value.startswith(\"/\"), f\"{path.name}: assert titles_in_order(read(out, \"announcements.html\")) == [\n        \"Written first\", \"Written third\", \"Written second\"]\n\n\ndef test_editing_after_publishing_does_not_reorder_and_shows_updated(db_path, tmp_path):\n    oldest = add_post(db_path, \"Oldest\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Middle\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Newest\")\n    before = titles_in_order(read(publish(db_path, tmp_path), \"announcements.html\"))\n    assert before == [\"Newest\", \"Middle\", \"Oldest\"]\n\n    posts.update(db_path, oldest, title=\"Oldest\", out = publish(db_path, tmp_path)\n    assert \"Updated\" not in read(out, \"posts/draft-polished-first.html\")\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a creates). Accounts sign in\nwith a username, not an email address.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import accounts\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"username\": \"admin\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"username\": \"editor\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n_TOKEN = re.compile(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"')\n\n\ndef csrf_token(client: TestClient, path: str = \"/login\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read the CSRF token from the form on `path` (what a browser would submit).\"\"\"\n    return token_in(client.get(path).text)\n\n\ndef token_in(html: str) -> str:\n    match = client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app(database=db_path))\n        response = c.post(\n            \"/login\",\n            data={\"username\": user[\"username\"], \"password\": user[\"password\"],\n                  \"csrf_token\": csrf_token(c)},\n            follow_redirects=False,\n        )\n        assert response.status_code in (302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nCreates the demo Admin (\"admin\") and Editor (\"editor\") if they do not exist, with\npasswords from CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD. As you build content\ntypes, extend this so it also creates:\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published (done: Posts and Pages)\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom contextlib import closing\n\nfrom app import accounts, pages, posts, settings\nfrom app.db import connect\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n seed_demo_pages(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    print(\"Demo accounts ready: 'admin' and 'editor' (passwords from your environment). \"\n          \"Demo Posts ready: one Published, one Draft. \"\n          \"Demo Pages ready: About ASA, Resources and Photos Published, one Draft.\")\n    return 0\n\n\n# Placeholders only: no claim about ASA's real events, dates, places or people.\nDEMO_POSTS = [\n    (\"Afrobeat event (demo placeholder)\", True,\n     \"This is a **demo placeholder**, not a real ASA announcement.\\n\\n\"\n     \"- **What:** an Afrobeat event\\n- **When:** to be announced\\n\"\n     \"- **Where:** to be announced\\n- **Who can attend:** to be announced\\n\"),\n    (\"Draft idea (demo placeholder)\", False,\n     \"A draft that must never appear on the public site.\\n\"),\n]\n\n\ndef seed_demo_posts(path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the demo Posts once, written by the demo Editor.\"\"\"\n    with closing(connect(path)) as conn:\n        if title, published, body in DEMO_POSTS:\n        post_id = posts.create(path, title=title, body=body, author_id=editor)\n        if published:\n            posts.publish(path, post_id)\n\n\n# Starter Pages: placeholders only, with no claim about ASA. Listed in Navigation order.\nDEMO_PAGES = [\n    (\"About ASA\", \"about-asa\", True,\n     \"This is a **demo placeholder** Page, not ASA's real About page.\\n\\n\"\n     \"ASA's own description of itself will replace this text.\\n\"),\n    (\"Resources\", \"resources\", True,\n     \"This is a **demo placeholder** Page, not a real list of ASA resources.\\n\\n\"\n     \"Cultural resources will be listed here.\\n\"),\n    (\"Photos\", \"photos\", True,\n     \"This is a **demo placeholder** Page.\\n\\n\"\n     \"Actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them.\\n\"),\n password = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n        if not password:\n            print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD in the environment (see .env.example).\")\n            return 1\n        try:\n The pieces already covered by the T03\ntests (five-item Home page, ordering, Updated dates) are not repeated here.\n\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport re\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\nfrom seed_demo.seed_demo_pages(db_path)\n\n\nclass Outline(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"The headings, images and landmarks of one HTML file, in document order.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, html):\n        super().__init__()\n        self.headings, self.images, self.tags, self.attrs = [], [], [], {}\n        self._open = None\n        self.feed(html)\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n seed_demo.seed_demo_pages(db_path)\n\n\nclass Outline(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"The headings, images and landmarks of one HTML file, in document order.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, html):\n        super().__init__()\n        self.headings, self.images, self.tags, self.attrs = [], [], [], {}\n        self._open = None\n        self.feed(html)\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n        self.tags.append(tag)\n        attrs = dict(attrs)\n        if tag == \"html\":\n            self.attrs[\"lang\"] = attrs.get(\"lang\")\n        if re.fullmatch(r\"h[1-6]\", tag):\n            self._open = [int(tag[1]), \"\"]\n        if tag == \"img\":\n            self.images.append(attrs)\n\n    def handle_data(self, data):\n        if self._open:\n            self._open[1] += data\n\n    def handle_endtag(self, tag):\n        if self._open and tag == f\"h{self._open[0]}\":\n            self.headings.append(tuple(self._open))\n            self._open = None\n\n    @property\n    def _tokens(block):\n    return dict(re.findall(r\"--([\\w-]+):\\s*(#[0-9a-fA-F]{6})\", block))\n\n\ndef _luminance(hex_colour):\n    channels = [int(hex_colour[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)]\n    r, g, b = [c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for c in channels]\n    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b\n\n\ndef contrast(a, b):\n    high, low = The one path for the public export and, later, Preview.\n\nRaw HTML is let through the Markdown parser and then removed by the sanitizer,\nso `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<form>` and event handlers never survive. Only\nheadings, emphasis, lists, links and images (with alt text) are kept.\n\nTwo things keep the page accessible whatever an Editor types: headings in a Body\nare moved below the page's own <h1> without skipping a level, and an image with\nno alt text gets a plain fallback instead of none.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\nimport nh3\n\n_markdown = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\", {\"html\": True})\n\n_TAGS = {\n    \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"p\", \"br\", \"em\", \"strong\",\n    \"ul\", \"ol\", \"li\", \"a\", \"img\",\n}\n_ATTRIBUTES = {\"a\": {\"href\", \"title\"}, \"img\": {\"src\", \"alt\", \"title\"}}\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"http\", \"https\", \"mailto\"}\n\n# Approved image files are copied to <site>/images/. An Editor always writes\n# `images/<file>`; each page adds the `root` that gets from there to the site root.\nIMAGES_FOLDER = \"images/\"\nNO_ALT = \"Image without a description\"\n\n_HEADING = re.compile(r\"<(/?)h([1-6])>\")\n_IMG_WITHOUT_ALT = re.compile(r\"<img(?![^>]*\\balt=)\")\n\n\ndef _attribute_filter(root: str):\n    def keep(tag: str, name: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Drop root-absolute links and images (the site is served from a\n        subfolder), point `images/...` at the site root, and never leave alt empty.\"\"\"\n        if name in (\"href\", \"src\") and value.strip().startswith(\"/\"):\n            return None\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"src\" and value.startswith(IMAGES_FOLDER):\n            return root + value\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"alt\" and not value.strip():\n            return NO_ALT\n        return value\n\n    return keep\n\n\ndef _nest_headings(html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Body headings start at <h2> and never skip a level.\n\n    The page's own title is the only <h1>. A heading may be at most one level\n    deeper than the one before it; siblings stay siblings.\n    \"\"\"\n    previous = 1\n    current = 2\n\n    def fix(match: re.Match) -> str:\n        nonlocal previous, current\n        if match.group(1):\n            return f\"</h{current}>\"\n        current = min(max(int(match.group(2)), 2), previous + 1)\n        previous = current\n        return f\"<h{current}>\"\n\n    return _HEADING.sub(fix, html)\n\n\ndef render_body(markdown: str, root: str = \"\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"`root` is the relative path from the page to the site root (\"\" or \"../\").\"\"\"\n    html = nh3.clean(\n        _markdown.render(markdown),\n        tags=_TAGS,\n        attributes=_ATTRIBUTES,\n        url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES,\n        clean_content_tags={\"script\", \"style\", \"iframe\", \"form\"},\n        attribute_filter=_attribute_filter(root),\n    )\n    html = _IMG_WITHOUT_ALT.sub(f'<img alt=\"{NO_ALT}\"', html)\n    return _nest_headings(html)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1858,"cache_read_input_tokens":87106,"output_tokens":5229,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":3573},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1858,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5229,"cache_read_input_tokens":87106,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1858,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1858},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_015LhDjW8UsmzhrTtogrBQee":{"file_path":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/rendering.py","content":"\"\"\"Markdown Body -> safe HTML. Only\nheadings, emphasis, lists, links and images (with alt text) are kept.\n\nTwo things keep the page accessible whatever an Editor types: headings in a Body\nare moved below the page's own <h1> without skipping a level, and an image with\nno alt text gets a plain fallback instead of none.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\nimport nh3\n\n_markdown = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\", {\"html\": True})\n\n_TAGS = {\n    \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"p\", \"br\", \"em\", \"strong\",\n    \"ul\", \"ol\", \"li\", \"a\", \"img\",\n}\n_ATTRIBUTES = {\"a\": {\"href\", \"title\"}, \"img\": {\"src\", \"alt\", \"title\"}}\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"http\", \"https\", \"mailto\"}\n\n# Approved image files are copied to <site>/images/. An Editor always writes\n# `images/<file>`; each page adds the `root` that gets from there to the site root.\nIMAGES_FOLDER = \"images/\"\nNO_ALT = \"Image without a description\"\n\n_HEADING = re.compile(r\"<(/?)h([1-6])>\")\n_IMG_WITHOUT_ALT = re.compile(r\"<img(?![^>]*\\balt=)\")\n\n\ndef _attribute_filter(root: str):\n    def keep(tag: str, name: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Drop root-absolute links and images (the site is served from a\n        subfolder), point `images/...` at the site root, and never leave alt empty.\"\"\"\n        if name in (\"href\", \"src\") and value.strip().startswith(\"/\"):\n            return None\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"src\" and value.startswith(IMAGES_FOLDER):\n            return root + value\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"alt\" and not value.strip():\n            return NO_ALT\n        return value\n\n    return keep\n\n\ndef _nest_headings(html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Body headings start at <h2> and never skip a level.\n\n    The page's own title is the only <h1>. A heading may be at most one level\n    deeper than the one before it; siblings stay siblings.\n    \"\"\"\n    previous = 1\n    current = 2\n\n    def fix(match: re.Match) -> str:\n        nonlocal previous, current\n        if match.group(1):\n            return f\"</h{current}>\"\n        current = min(max(int(match.group(2)), 2), previous + 1)\n        previous = current\n        return f\"<h{current}>\"\n\n    return _HEADING.sub(fix, html)\n\n\ndef render_body(markdown: str, root: str = \"\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"`root` is the relative path from the page to the site root (\"\" or \"../\").\"\"\"\n    html = nh3.clean(\n        _markdown.render(markdown),\n        tags=_TAGS,\n        attributes=_ATTRIBUTES,\n        url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES,\n        clean_content_tags={\"script\", \"style\", \"iframe\", \"form\"},\n        attribute_filter=_attribute_filter(root),\n    )\n    html = _IMG_WITHOUT_ALT.sub(f'<img alt=\"{NO_ALT}\"', html)\n    return _nest_headings(html)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":3,"oldLines":9,"newStart":3,"newLines":15,"lines":[" Raw HTML is let through the Markdown parser and then removed by the sanitizer,"," so `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<form>` and event handlers never survive. }\n\nhtml { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; }\n\nbody {\n  margin: 0;\n  background: var(--bg);\n  color: var(--text);\n  font: 1.0625rem/1.65 system-ui, -apple-system, \"Segoe UI\", sans-serif;\n  overflow-wrap: anywhere;\n}\n\nimg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }\n\na { color: var(--link); text-underline-offset: 0.15em; }\na:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 0.15em; }\n\n:focus-visible {\n  outline: 3px solid var(--focus);\n  outline-offset: 3px;\n  border-radius: 2px;\n}\n\n.skip-link {\n  position: absolute;\n  left: 1rem;\n  top: -4rem;\n  z-index: 10;\n  padding: 0.6rem 1rem;\n  background: var(--accent);\n  color: var(--on-accent);\n  font-weight: 700;\n}\n.skip-link:focus { top: 0.5rem; }\n\n/* Header: a decorative colour band, the site name, then the Navigation. */\n.site-header { border-top: 0.5rem solid var(--band-1); border-image: linear-gradient(\n  to right, var(--band-1) 0 33%, var(--band-2) 33% 66%, var(--band-3) 66% 100%) 1; }\n.site-header-inner { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0.75rem 1rem 0; }\n.site-name {\n  display: inline-block;\n  padding: 0.4rem 0;\n  color: var(--text);\n  font-size: 1.15rem;\n  font-weight: 800;\n  text-decoration: none;\n}\n.site-nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem 0.5rem; margin: 0 -0.5rem; }\n.site-nav a {\n  display: inline-block;\n  padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem;          /* a comfortable touch target */\n  color: var(--text);\n  font-weight: 600;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;\n}\n.site-nav a:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--line); }\n.site-nav a[aria-current=\"page\"] { color: var(--link); border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }\n\nmain { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 1.5rem 1rem 2.5rem; }\nmain:focus { outline: none; }   /* only the skip link moves focus here; nothing to show */\n\nh1 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1.9rem; line-height: 1.2; }\nh2 { margin: 2rem 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1.45rem; line-height: 1.25; }\nh3 { margin: 1.5rem 0 0.5rem; font-size: 1.2rem; line-height: 1.3; }\nh4, h5, h6 { margin: 1.25rem 0 0.5rem; font-size: 1.05rem; }\n\n.hero {\n  margin-bottom: 1.5rem;\n  padding: 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.5rem;\n  background: var(--surface);\n  border: 1px solid var(--line);\n  border-left: 0.5rem solid var(--accent);\n  border-radius: 0.5rem;\n}\n.welcome { margin: 0; font-size: 1.15rem; }\n\n.cards { margin-block: 1rem; }\n.card {\n  margin-block: 1rem;\n  padding: 1rem 1.1rem;\n  background: var(--surface);\n  border: 1px solid var(--line);\n  border-radius: 0.5rem;\n}\n.card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.3; }\n.card-title a { color: var(--text); text-decoration-color: var(--accent); }\n.card-title a:hover { color: var(--link); }\n.meta { margin: 0.35rem 0 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.95rem; }\n\n.more {\n  display: inline-block;\n  margin-top: 0.5rem;\n  padding: 0.7rem 1.1rem;\n  background: var(--accent);\n  color: var(--on-accent);\n  font-weight: 700;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  border-radius: 0.4rem;\n}\n.more:hover { text-decoration: underline; }\n\n.body > :first-child { margin-top: 0; }\n.body img { display: block; margin-block: 1rem 0.25rem; border-radius: 0.4rem; }\n.body em { color: var(--muted); }\n.body ul, .body ol { padding-left: 1.4rem; }\n\n.back { margin-top: 2rem; }\n\nfooter { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 1rem 1rem 2rem; color: var(--muted); border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }\n\n@media (min-width: 40rem) {\n  h1 { font-size: 2.3rem; {"parentUuid":"ba895ab3-9c5b-4da8-bd84-31ee65c4a9f1","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b4782d42-f54b-404f-bbf6-049a33d49a2c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yawoppong-krampah/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: HEAD (uncommitted T07 work for issue #8)"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"d3ba9e0c-41d0-49ea-a4fd-283825751699","timestamp":"2026-10-12T07:15:16.876Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01EkUkDKnNp8YP5cpfN7Dopq","session_id":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c05c18e7-34e7-496f-8714-9639bdc19adf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"main"}

The only post-clean changes are the `&lt;img alt&gt;` regex and the heading re-levelling, and neither adds attributes from user input. The test also uses `p.suffix` without `.lower()`, unlike `copy_images`.\n2. **Duplicated Code:** the nav regex and tag-stripping are repeated in the tests. `re.search(r'&lt;nav aria-label=\"Main\"&gt;(.*?)&lt;/nav&gt;'…)` appears twice, and `re.sub(r\"&lt;[^&gt;]+&gt;\", \" \", …)` appears four times. In the `fix` callback, `current` is also reused for closing tags. Names like `last_level` and `open_level` would be clearer.\n4. **Mysterious Name:** `Outline.attrs` only ever holds `lang`. Use `self.lang`.\n5. **Primitive Obsession (mild):** `root` is a bare string (`\"\"` or `\"../\"`) that is passed to both `render_body` and the templates.\n6. **Speculative Generality (mild):** `card_level|default(2)` in `_card.html` builds the heading tag dynamically. It is only needed for Home, which uses `card_level=3`. `render_site` also now takes an `images` parameter, which tests need but production never overrides.\n7. **Feature Envy (mild):** `render_site` reads `settings.TEMPLATES / \"public\" / \"style.css\"` directly. The path knowledge could move into `settings`, as `IMAGES` did.\n8. **Divergent Change (mild):** `app/rendering.py` now sanitizes, rewrites image paths, and re-levels headings. Accessibility is a separate reason to change from sanitization. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**T07 spec review: 24/24 tests in `tests/test_t07_public_site.py` pass. Every acceptance criterion in #8 is met in substance; below are the gaps, scope creep and weak spots.**\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Photos page content lives only in the seed.** The ticket says \"The Photos page shows placeholder or rights-cleared demo images labelled as illustrative…\". `seed_demo_pages` returns early if any Page exists (`scripts/seed_demo.py:94-96`). An existing demo DB therefore never gets the illustrations or captions, and a real Photos page won't have them either. The test passes only because it re-seeds a fresh DB.\n- **\"Keeps its original First-published date and position\" is only half-tested.** The new `test_republishing_keeps_the_original_first_published_date` uses a single Post, so it can't show position. T03's `test_a_post_unpublished_and_republished_keeps_its_place` covers position, and I did not re-run it separately.\n- **Home five-item cap and link are tested only in T03.** The ticket's last criterion lists them under T07 tests. They exist (`test_home_shows_the_five_latest_and_links_to_all_announcements`), but T07 re-asserts none. T07's own card tests use one Post.\n- **No test or script enforces about 390 px.** The CSS test only checks `max-width:100%` and that no fixed `px` width exceeds 390. Screenshots exist, but nothing re-checks them.\n- **Image references other than `images/&lt;file&gt;` are not resolved.** `../images/x.png` and `./images/x.png` are left as written (`app/rendering.py` `_attribute_filter`). Both break under `posts/`, and `./images/x.png` breaks at the root too.\n\n**(b) Scope creep, mild**\n- **Dark colour scheme.** `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` plus a second contrast table. The ticket asked only for \"readable colour contrast\".\n- **Extras.** `aria-current`, a skip link and `main tabindex=-1` all support keyboard access. The extension allow-list and hidden-file filter in `copy_images` is defensible hardening, but it is not in the ticket.\n- **Red/gold/green header band.** It reads as decoration and is not a claim. Still, it is a design choice nobody specified.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but is wrong or fragile**\n- **Alt-text fallback undermines the rule.** The spec says \"Every photo has descriptive alt text\" (CONTEXT.md, Photo). `render_body` silently substitutes `\"Image without a description\"` for missing or empty alt (`NO_ALT`). The \"alt text on every image\" test then passes on that placeholder. This hides an Editor error instead of surfacing it, and it is not descriptive alt text.\n- **Alt-detection regex can be fooled.** `&lt;img(?![^&gt;]*\\balt=)` will treat `title=\"alt=…\"` as alt present, so that image gets no fallback.\n- **`render_body(markdown, root=\"\")` default breaks the Preview.** The spec says \"The same rendering and sanitizing path is used for the admin preview and the public export\". The Preview does not call `render_body` yet. When it does, `images/…` will resolve against the admin URL and show broken images unless the Preview passes a root.\n- **Captions are plain italic paragraphs, not tied to the images.** The label is `*Illustrative placeholder, not a photo of a real ASA event.*`. It is not a `&lt;figure&gt;/&lt;figcaption&gt;`. The tests count the word \"illustrative\" and do not check that a label sits next to each image.\n- **The \"no claim beyond the brief\" test is a short keyword denylist.** It only looks for strings like \"founded\" and \"weekly\". It would not catch other claims, though the seed copy I read contains none.\n- **Tests that pass `images=None` fall back to the real `settings.IMAGES`.** They are not isolated from the repo's `images/` folder.\n\n**Checked and fine**\n- **Welcome text:** the wording matches the brief exactly.\n- **Event cards:** they show title, \"Posted\" date, byline and \"Updated\", and never say \"event date\".\n- **Posts and Pages:** Post images resolve with `../`, root Page images with no prefix, and there are no absolute paths or Drafts in the export.\n- **Headings:** there is one `h1` and no skipped levels, and Body headings are demoted below it.\n- **Photos page:** it has the \"actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them\" sentence.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>61878</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>8</tool_uses><duration_ms>46271</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"c7217abe-aa1e-4aa7-ae2e-aacdea8b0133","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfww9NTBYuWBciAV3WKjN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T07 (#8) is committed as `b29a37c` on `main`, and all 309 tests pass (280 before, 29 new). I haven't pushed, so issue #8 is still open; once you push, the `Closes #8` line will close it. At 390px the home and photos pages lay out cleanly. I checked this in headless Chrome and saved the screenshots as `docs/screenshots/T07-home-390px.png` and `T07-photos-390px.png`.\n\n**What changed:**\n- **Home and cards:** the Welcome text uses only the client brief's wording, with a hero panel above the five latest Event cards and an \"All announcements\" link.\n- **Styling:** the public stylesheet is now `templates/public/style.css`. It has light and dark colour sets, and the tests check text contrast. It also adds a skip link, visible focus and a marker on the current page in the menu.\n- **Images:** `cms publish` copies approved image files from a new `images/` folder into the site. A reference like `images/x.png` works from both Posts and Pages, and `./images/` and `../images/` forms are accepted too.\n- **Headings and alt text:** headings inside a Body are moved below the page title without skipping a level. An image with no alt text gets a fallback.\n- **Photos page:** the demo Photos page shows three original illustrations I drew. Each is labelled as illustrative and not a photo of a real ASA event, and the page says actual event photos will be added once ASA has permission.\n\n**Review:** the Standards and Spec reviews found no hard violations. I fixed what was cheap and real, and posted the findings and their resolutions on issue #8, as `CLAUDE.md` asks.\n\n**Things to know:**\n- **Existing `cms.db`:** `seed_demo.py` skips Pages that already exist, so your current Photos page won't pick up the illustrations. Edit its body as Admin or rebuild the database.\n- **Alt fallback:** the fallback text (\"Image without a description\") doesn't tell the Editor they left alt text out. T08's Preview is the place to show that, and the Preview will also need to pass the right image path root.\n- **Uncommitted files:** `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and the new transcripts are still uncommitted, as before."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":467,"cache_read_input_tokens":132528,"output_tokens":767,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":30},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":467,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":767,"cache_read_input_tokens":132528,"cache_creation_input_tokens":467,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":467},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfww9N8pykQNmxb8aw4pG","type":"assistant","uuid":"087f6867-e5d4-491e-8471-3ee31c881cde","timestamp":"2026-10-12T07:17:38.074Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c05c18e7-34e7-496f-8714-9639bdc19adf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"main"}
